answer: A newcomer earns standing by tending a vine cutting planted on a dune, logging its growth — photo, height, and soil reading — at three stages, the last when the vine reaches its zenith. Two vineyard keepers verify the log against nursery records within six days, checking height against known growth and soil against the dune. A copied photo, a height the vine could not reach, or a missing stage voids the season, burns the 50-credit stake and bars the sponsor a year. One honest season costs 50 credits; a thousand fakes need 1,000 stakes and 1,000 seasons of vine logs, each checked at the dune.
